title: Equation of a circle
examples: How do I find the equation if I know the centre and radius?
What is the formula for a tangent line to a circle?
Can you show me how completing the square works with a circle equation?

explain.say: Today we learn the equation of a circle. The standard form is very useful. It is x minus a squared plus y minus b squared equals r squared.
The numbers a and b give you the centre point. The centre is at a comma b. The number r is the radius. Remember r squared is the right side.
Sometimes the equation needs fixing. This is when we complete the square. It helps us find the centre and radius. We work with x squared and y squared terms.
If a line touches the circle at only one point, it is a tangent. The radius line is always perpendicular to the tangent line there. This is key.

faq.q: What do a and b represent in the equation?
faq.a: The values a and b are the coordinates of the centre of the circle. They tell you exactly where the circle is located on the graph.

faq.q: What is the difference between r and r squared?
faq.a: R is the actual distance from the centre to the edge. R squared is that distance multiplied by itself. You must use r squared in the equation.
asks: Do I use r or r squared?
What goes on the right side?

faq.q: When do I need to complete the square?
faq.a: You need to complete the square when the equation is not in the standard form. It helps you rearrange it to find the centre and radius.
asks: When is completing the square necessary?
How do I put it in standard form?

faq.q: How do I find the equation of a tangent line?
faq.a: You usually find the gradient of the radius first. Then, the tangent line has the negative reciprocal gradient. You use the point of contact.
asks: How do I find the tangent?

faq.q: Does the equation change if the circle is centred at the origin?
faq.a: Yes, if the centre is at the origin, then a and b are both zero. The equation simplifies to x squared plus y squared equals r squared.
asks: Is it simpler if a and b are zero?

facts: The standard equation of a circle is (x minus a) squared plus (y minus b) squared equals r squared.
The point (a, b) is always the centre of the circle.
A tangent line touches the circle at exactly one point.
The radius drawn to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

quiz.say: If the equation is x squared plus y squared equals 25, what is the centre?
quiz.why: The equation matches the form where a and b are both zero, so the centre is the origin.

wrong.1: This is tempting because you might think the radius is 5, making the centre (5, 0).
wrong.2: This is tempting because you might assume the centre is at the y-axis intercept.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might incorrectly use the radius value for both coordinates.

quiz.say: What is the radius squared if the centre is (2, -3) and the equation is (x-2)² + (y+3)² = 16?
quiz.why: The right side of the standard equation is always r squared, which is given as 16.

wrong.1: This is tempting because you might only read the x-coordinate of the centre.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you might only read the y-coordinate of the centre.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might add the absolute values of the centre coordinates.

quiz.say: A circle has its centre at (1, 4) and is tangent to the line y equals 1. What is the radius?
quiz.why: The radius is the vertical distance between the centre y-coordinate of 4 and the tangent line y=1. The distance is 4 minus 1, which is 3.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you might mistake the centre's y-coordinate for the radius.
wrong.1: This is tempting because you might calculate the distance from the centre to the origin.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might confuse the x-coordinate of the centre with the radius.
